note: Unselected T2DM; five SGLT2 inhibitors went to patients on ZDF-rat and db/db-mouse glucosuria and HbA1c data that held, while the rat toxicology calls on bone and tumours did not transfer.
label: T2DM (SGLT2 inhibitors)

engagement.judgement: Opener only: phlorizin is not a member (non-selective SGLT1/2), so product_in_model is false and nothing scores.
engagement.note: Phlorizin, the non-selective SGLT progenitor, lowered glycaemia by glucosuria in 90%-pancreatectomized rats: the readout the class later used.
engagement.quote: These data demonstrate that a reduction of beta-cell mass leads to the development of insulin resistance, and correction of hyperglycemia with phlorizin, without change in insulin levels, normalizes insulin sensitivity.

engagement.magnitude_basis: RTG floor under canagliflozin: ZDF rat 94 mg/dL (from 415) vs healthy men ~60 mg/dL (from ~180-240)
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Liang 2012 (epub 2012-02-15) is the model side and sets the year; Sha 2011 preceded it. The FDA 2013 ClinPharm review records the same dose-dependent RTG fall in T2DM patients (study NAP-1002).
engagement.judgement: Paired comparison, not stated by either paper. RTG/UGE is the transporter's own flux, so proximal, not direct. Healthy volunteers count for engagement. The ZDF RTG studies (DD10318/DD10319) are in the FDA pharmacology review, so model_filed is true.
engagement.note: Canagliflozin 1 mg/kg cut rat RTG from 415 to 94 mg/dL; in healthy men it cut RTG dose-dependently to about 60 mg/dL.
engagement.short: Rat RTG drop reproduced in men
engagement.quote: Dose dependently, canagliflozin decreased calculated 24-h mean RT(G) with maximal reduction to approximately 60 mg/dl, and increased mean 24-h UGE.
engagement.reason: Rat RTG drop reproduced in humans

engagement.note: Genetic loss of Sglt2 in mice gave a 500-fold glucosuria; no drug and nobody had yet compared it with dosed humans.
engagement.quote: SGLT2 deletion resulted in a threefold increase in urine output and a 500-fold increase in glucosuria, as well as compensatory increases in feeding, drinking, and activity.
engagement.judgement: Opener at first use (Ly 2011 print January, Jurczak 2011 print March). A knockout carries no drug, so product_in_model false; the canagliflozin pharmacology review names no Sglt2-null mouse (grep: knockout, Sweet Pee, KO), so model_filed false.
engagement.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

engagement.magnitude_basis: direction of urinary glucose excretion: 500-fold glucosuria in Sglt2-null mice vs dose-dependent 24-h UGE rise in healthy men
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level for both papers. Sha 2011 has no epub date on Europe PMC (print July 2011) and its phase 1 study was not found on a registry; registry_date null.
engagement.note: The glucosuria the null mouse shows appeared dose-dependently in healthy men on canagliflozin, with the renal glucose threshold falling to about 60 mg/dl.
engagement.short: Null-mouse glucosuria seen in dosed men
engagement.quote: Dose dependently, canagliflozin decreased calculated 24-h mean RT(G) with maximal reduction to approximately 60 mg/dl, and increased mean 24-h UGE.
engagement.reason: Null-mouse glucosuria seen in dosed men
engagement.judgement: Paired: the knockout's glucosuria (Jurczak 2011, March) against the canagliflozin phase 1 UGE rise (Sha 2011, July); both public in 2011, so the year is 2011. Proximal readout (urinary glucose, the transporter's own substrate). Direction only: a null allele is not a dose.
engagement.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

dose.judgement: Opener only; phlorizin is not a member.
dose.note: Rat exposure-response for glucosuria existed from phlorizin; no human exposure target was set until canagliflozin.
dose.quote: Phlorizin treatment of diabetic rats completely normalized insulin sensitivity but had no effect on insulin action in controls.

dose.magnitude_basis: effective dose: ZDF rat 1 mg/kg (RTG) vs human 100 mg (~1.4 mg/kg), where the ClinPharm review says RTG plateaus
dose.judgement: Decision 16: a stated margin (5-7x for renal/adrenal tumours; 12x at the tumour dose) held, and the human dose reached the RTG plateau ('decreased in a dose-dependent manner with doses up to 100 mg and was almost similar at doses higher than 100 mg', ClinPharm review). The Leydig-cell tumours had no margin but never appeared in patients; that harm is counted once, in safety, not here. registry_date is CANTATA-M results posting (NCT01081834).
dose.model: ZDF rat efficacy exposure with SD-rat/dog toxicology margins
dose.note: Human 100/300 mg sat on the RTG plateau; rat renal/adrenal tumour exposures lay 5-7x above, and patients reached target without them.
dose.short: Dosed to target inside stated margin
dose.quote: For canagliflozin, significant carbohydrate malabsorption or calcium imbalance did not occur in clinical trials, and a 5- to 7-fold safety margin exists for the renal tubular and adrenal malignancies observed in rats.

dose.note: Rat PK was scaled to a human clearance, volume and bioavailability prediction to set the first-in-human dose of ertugliflozin.
dose.short: Rat allometry set the FIH dose
dose.quote: Single-species allometric scaling of rat pharmacokinetics of PF-04971729 was used to predict human clearance, distribution volume, and oral bioavailability.
dose.judgement: Opener at first use. model_filed is set from a grep of the combined 2017 ertugliflozin pharmacology review (NDA 209803/209805/209806) for 'allometr'.
dose.model: Single-species allometric scaling of rat pharmacokinetics to predict human clearance, volume and bioavailability (ertugliflozin, PF-04971729)

dose.magnitude_basis: predicted vs observed human clearance, volume and bioavailability; the abstract gives no numbers, so the fold-error is not recorded
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only; predicted and observed values not read. The first-in-human single-ascending-dose study is NCT00989079 (first posted 2009-10-02, healthy volunteers) with no results posted, so registry_date is null.
dose.note: First-in-human PK fell in the range the rat-scaled prediction gave for a low daily dose; 5 and 15 mg later succeeded in phase 3.
dose.short: FIH PK matched the rat-scaled prediction
dose.quote: First-in-human studies after oral administration indicated that the human pharmacokinetics/dose predictions for PF-04971729 were in the range that is likely to yield a favorable pharmacodynamic response.
dose.reason: FIH PK matched the rat-scaled prediction
dose.judgement: Dose: the model's exposure target was reached in healthy volunteers and the source itself states the comparison (comparison_stated true). Scored same under 'reached' with healthy-volunteer PK counting; the 2017 phase 3 approval later confirmed the dose was enough, which changes no status. No tolerability margin was stated, so margin_stated false. A reviewer may judge routine allometric scaling out of scope as a model system; it is kept because the brief asks for in-silico dose models compared with human PK, and this is the only member whose own dose prediction is published with its outcome.
dose.model: Single-species allometric scaling of rat pharmacokinetics to predict human clearance, volume and bioavailability (ertugliflozin, PF-04971729)

efficacy.judgement: Opener only; phlorizin is not a member and nothing scores.
efficacy.note: Phlorizin normalized glycaemia and insulin sensitivity in 90%-pancreatectomized rats; the model the class was built on.
efficacy.quote: Phlorizin treatment of diabetic rats completely normalized insulin sensitivity but had no effect on insulin action in controls.

efficacy.judgement: A human-genetic track: FRG carriers are non-diabetic, so they predict glucosuria and its tolerability, not an HbA1c effect; nobody compared them with trial HbA1c before 2021.
efficacy.model: People with SLC5A2 loss-of-function (familial renal glucosuria)
efficacy.note: SLC5A2 loss-of-function carriers show lifelong glucosuria without hypoglycaemia; cited as rationale (Zhang 2011) but never compared on HbA1c.
efficacy.quote: Fourteen individuals (including the original patient with 'renal glucosuria type 0') were homozygous or compound heterozygous for an SGLT2 mutation resulting in glucosuria in the range of 14.6 to 202 g/1.73 m(2)/d (81 - 1120 mmol/1.73 m(2)/d).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c change; the ZDF rat number is not in the Liang 2012 abstract
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Liang 2012 and Stenlof 2013; the rat HbA1c effect size was not read.
efficacy.judgement: Paired: Liang 2012 (ZDF HbA1c fell) against the CANTATA-M primary endpoint. No member fell below the class bar in the model and failed, so no 'neg'. outcome_tested is positive on CANVAS (MACE HR 0.86, 2017) and CREDENCE (renal, 2019). registry_date is CANTATA-M results posting; epub 2013-01-24 is earlier and sets the year.
efficacy.note: Canagliflozin lowered HbA1c in ZDF rats over 4 weeks; CANTATA-M met its HbA1c primary endpoint, and CANVAS later showed MACE benefit.
efficacy.short: Rat HbA1c drop matched in CANTATA-M
efficacy.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).

patient_trials.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).

The rate of the primary outcome was lower with canagliflozin than with placebo (occurring in 26.9 vs. 31.5 participants per 1000 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.97; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.02 for superiority).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction of the HbA1c and heart-failure associations vs the SGLT2-inhibitor trial effects
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract only. General-population genetics (UK Biobank, mostly non-diabetic), not T2DM patients; HbA1c appears as a mediator, heart failure is the headline; the abstract frames the analysis against SGLT2-inhibitor trials but the full text was not read.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (2021, after CANTATA-M 2013 and CANVAS 2017), so retro, never same. Scored at class level on direction only; a reviewer may prefer to drop it to untested because the model side is not a T2DM population.
efficacy.model: People with SLC5A2 loss-of-function (familial renal glucosuria)
efficacy.note: A SLC5A2 expression-lowering genetic score tracked lower HbA1c and lower heart-failure risk in UK Biobank, after the trials.
efficacy.quote: Two intronic SNPs associated with SLC5A2 expression were included in a genetic score, which was associated with lower risk of heart failure in UK Biobank (odds ratio 0.97, 95% confidence interval, 0.95-0.99, P = 0.016).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: HbA1c; the db/db and ZDF effect sizes (review Figure 3) were not read
efficacy.confidence_note: Review read by grep; the review states the rodent HbA1c effect occurred 'at exposures equivalent to the clinical dose'. Registry date for C-450 not looked up.
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2013 call with a second member (bexagliflozin = EGT1442; Zhang 2011 is the db/db model paper). The smaller human effect (-0.4%) is not a failure, so no 'neg'.
efficacy.model: db/db mouse and ZDF rat 4-week HbA1c
efficacy.note: FDA: bexagliflozin cut HbA1c in db/db mice and ZDF rats at exposures equivalent to the clinical dose; patients: -0.4% (monotherapy) and -0.5% (add-on).
efficacy.quote: with a placebo-adjusted change from baseline in HbA1c of -0.4% (-0.6%, -0.1%; p=0.002) in C-450, and as add-on to metformin, with a placebo-adjusted change from baseline in HbA1c of -0.5% (-0.7%, -0.3%; p<0.0001) in C-419

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the JASN full text was not retrievable from Europe PMC.
efficacy.note: Sweet Pee (Slc5a2 nonsense) mice kept better glycaemic control after STZ diabetes; no drug, no patient comparison yet.
efficacy.quote: After induction of diabetes, Sweet Pee mice had better overall glycemic control than wild-type control mice, but had a higher risk for infection and an increased mortality rate (70% in homozygous mutants versus 10% in controls at 20 weeks).
efficacy.judgement: Opener at first use. Ly 2011 compares the mutant with familial renal glucosuria patients, not with drug-treated patients, so this is not a stated model-vs-trial comparison.
efficacy.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

efficacy.magnitude_basis: direction only: fasting hyperglycaemia prevented in db/db Sglt2-null mice vs HbA1c -0.77/-1.03% vs placebo at week 26 (CANTATA-M)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Jurczak 2011 and Stenlof 2013. registry_date is the CANTATA-M results posting (2013-06-03, checked by the tile's checker); the first-posted date is in patient_trials.

patient_trials.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).

The rate of the primary outcome was lower with canagliflozin than with placebo (occurring in 26.9 vs. 31.5 participants per 1000 patient-years; hazard ratio, 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.75 to 0.97; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.02 for superiority).

efficacy.note: Sglt2 deletion prevented fasting hyperglycaemia in db/db mice; canagliflozin lowered HbA1c by 0.77-1.03% vs placebo at 26 weeks in CANTATA-M.
efficacy.short: Null-mouse glycaemia matched by HbA1c fall
efficacy.quote: At week 26, HbA1c was significantly reduced from baseline with canagliflozin 100 and 300 mg compared with placebo (-0.77, -1.03 and 0.14%, respectively; p < 0.001 for both).
efficacy.reason: Null-mouse glycaemia matched by HbA1c fall
efficacy.judgement: Paired, prospective: the 2011 genetic model preceded the 2013 primary-endpoint result. Scored direction only because a null allele sets no effect size for a drug. outcome_tested positive on CANVAS 2017 (status unchanged, listed in patient_trials as the tile does).
efficacy.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

safety.judgement: Human-genetic track opener. The FDA 2013 pharmacology and medical reviews do not mention familial renal glucosuria, so model_filed is false.
safety.model: People with SLC5A2 loss-of-function (familial renal glucosuria)
safety.note: FRG carriers excrete 15-200 g glucose/day with no hypoglycaemia; the 'benign' phenotype was never set against trial harms.
safety.quote: Fourteen individuals (including the original patient with 'renal glucosuria type 0') were homozygous or compound heterozygous for an SGLT2 mutation resulting in glucosuria in the range of 14.6 to 202 g/1.73 m(2)/d (81 - 1120 mmol/1.73 m(2)/d).

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Left untested by choice: 'no hypoglycaemia' held in trials, but 'no other obvious morbidity' rests on 14 carriers and cannot be called a prediction about a 5-10% genital-infection rate or rare DKA; no admissible source made the comparison.
safety.judgement: Judgement call: neither same nor contra. A held prediction (no hypoglycaemia) and a contradicted silence (genital mycotic infections, DKA) would need a source that puts the FRG cohort beside trial harms; none found, and pairing a 14-person case series against AE rates is not a comparison.
safety.model: People with SLC5A2 loss-of-function (familial renal glucosuria)
safety.note: The bexagliflozin discovery paper used FRG as its safety rationale; no source compares that phenotype with DKA or genital mycotic infection rates.
safety.quote: Human subjects with homozygous or compound heterozygous mutations in SLC5A2 exhibit glucosuria without hypoglycemia or other obvious morbidity
safety.reason: No source compared FRG with trial harms

safety.magnitude_basis: bone: rat trabecular accretion and hypercalciuria 'at clinically relevant exposure' vs no calcium disruption or accretion in patients
safety.judgement: Decision 13: judged on what the rat data showed, not the sponsor's SGLT1-malabsorption explanation. The review says the bone effects came 'at clinically relevant exposure' and Leydig tumours 'at all doses tested with no safety margin'; the medical review states 'Pheochromocytoma or Leydig cell tumors have not been reported thus far'. A predicted harm that never appeared is contra/opposite. DKA: rats showed raised urinary ketones at 20-100 mg/kg but the review drew no ketoacidosis prediction; 3 DKA cases sat in the phase 3 table and the 2015 FDA warning followed, an unpredicted harm noted here, not scored separately.
safety.model: Rat 2-year carcinogenicity and chronic toxicology (SD rat, CD-1 mouse, dog)
safety.note: Rats predicted calcium disruption, bone accretion and Leydig tumours at clinical exposure; patients showed none, and rats were silent on DKA.
safety.short: Rat bone and tumour calls missed
safety.quote: at the therapeutic doses of 100 and 300mg, canagliflozin did not result in carbohydrate malabsorption (e.g., negative hydrogen breath tests), calcium disruption (e.g., vit D, PTH levels), or bone accretion in clinical trials

safety.magnitude_basis: direction of bone change: rat trabecular accretion vs human total-hip BMD -0.9/-1.2% and more fractures in CANVAS (4.0% vs 2.6%, Watts 2016, doi 10.1210/jc.2015-3167)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level for Bilezikian 2016 and Watts 2016 (both epub 2015-11-18). registry_date is the results posting of NCT01106651 (the older-adults study that carried the DXA substudy).
safety.judgement: Paired: FDA pharmacology review (rat bone accretion) against the DXA substudy. The human bone harm the rat flagged ran in the opposite direction, so the 2013 contra stands and is strengthened; fractures are mentioned in note via Watts 2016, not given their own entry.
safety.model: Rat 2-year carcinogenicity and chronic toxicology (SD rat, CD-1 mouse, dog)
safety.note: Patients lost total-hip BMD (-0.9/-1.2% vs placebo over 104 weeks) and CANVAS fractures rose (Watts 2016): the opposite of rat hyperostosis.
safety.short: Human bone loss, not rat accretion
safety.quote: Canagliflozin doses of 100 and 300 mg were associated with a decrease in total hip BMD over 104 weeks, (placebo-subtracted changes: -0.9% and -1.2%, respectively), but not at other sites measured (femoral neck, lumbar spine, or distal forearm).

safety.magnitude_basis: rodent Leydig-cell tumour and pheochromocytoma vs zero cases in the bexagliflozin program
safety.confidence_note: Review read by grep; bexagliflozin's own rat carcinogenicity findings were not read, and the review notes few events limit interpretability for renal cell carcinoma.
safety.judgement: Strengthens with a second member. The review compares the class's rodent tumour signals (raised at canagliflozin approval) with the bexagliflozin clinical database and finds none; it calls renal cell carcinoma uninterpretable on few events, hence source_calls_it unresolved.
safety.model: Rat 2-year carcinogenicity and chronic toxicology (SD rat, CD-1 mouse, dog)
safety.note: A second member's program: the class's rodent Leydig-cell and pheochromocytoma signals again produced no cases in patients.
safety.short: No rodent tumour types in bexagliflozin patients
safety.quote: No events of Leydig cell tumor or pheochromocytoma were observed in the bexagliflozin clinical program.
safety.reason: Rat tumour and bone calls never transferred

safety.note: The Sweet Pee authors predicted infection, malnutrition, volume contraction and mortality risks from SGLT2 inhibition before any phase 3 result.
safety.quote: Our model suggests that inhibiting SGLT2 may improve glucose control but may confer increased risks for infection, malnutrition, volume contraction, and mortality.
safety.judgement: Opener at first use; the prediction was stated in January 2011, two years before the canagliflozin label.
safety.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

safety.magnitude_basis: direction of adverse-reaction rates vs placebo in the 2013 label: female genital mycotic infection 10.4/11.4% vs 3.2%, UTI 5.9/4.3% vs 4.0%, dose-dependent volume-depletion reactions; mortality not raised (pooled CV death HR 0.65, MACE HR 0.98 in the FDA summary review)
safety.confidence_note: Label and summary review read by grep; the label's adverse-reaction table pools four placebo-controlled 26-week trials, so registry_date is the CANTATA-M results posting (NCT01081834, 2013-06-03), one of the four. Mortality figure is the FDA summary review's nine-trial pooled CV analysis (CV death HR 0.65, 0.34-1.24).
safety.note: Infection and volume contraction appeared in the 2013 label (genital mycotic 10.4-11.4% vs 3.2%); the mutant's 70% mortality did not appear in patients.
safety.short: Infection and volume calls held, mortality not
safety.quote: INVOKANA increases the risk of genital mycotic infections.
safety.reason: Infection and volume calls held, mortality not
safety.judgement: Partial agreement scored same with source_calls_it partial, per the brief: two of the four predicted harms (infection, volume contraction) held in the label and three of the four if weight loss stands in for malnutrition; the mortality call did not (no excess in the pooled phase 2/3 CV analysis). A reviewer applying 'a predicted harm that never appeared is contra, magnitude opposite' to the mortality call alone would flip this track to contra; the mortality signal came from STZ-diabetic homozygous mutants, an insulin-deficient setting unlike unselected T2DM, which is why it is read as a partial match here. Scored at the 2013 label, before CANVAS.
safety.model: Slc5a2-null mouse (Sweet Pee nonsense mutant; Sglt2 knockout on chow, high-fat, db/db or STZ backgrounds)

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the Bone full text (PMC4679447) was not retrievable from Europe PMC.
safety.note: A diabetic-bone-disease mouse dosed with canagliflozin for 10 weeks, run after the 2013 label already carried the fracture signal.
safety.quote: Canagliflozin treatment improved BG in DM mice by ~35%, but did not improve microarchitectural parameters.
safety.judgement: Opener at first use (epub 2015-07-23). Post-approval academic study, so model_filed false.
safety.model: DBA/2J male mouse, STZ-diabetic and control, 10-week canagliflozin in chow; microCT, bone strength and resorption markers

safety.magnitude_basis: direction of bone change: trabecular loss and a higher resorption marker in mice vs total-hip BMD -0.9/-1.2% (Bilezikian 2016) and fracture 18.7/17.6 vs 14.2 per 1000 patient-years in the 2013 label
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. registry_date is the results posting of NCT01106651 (the older-adults study carrying the DXA substudy), as used by the tile's 2015 rodent-tox entry; the patient side (2013 label, Bilezikian 2016) is already in the tile.
safety.note: Canagliflozin cost control mice trabecular bone and raised a resorption marker in diabetic mice: the human direction (BMD loss, fractures), reproduced after the fact.
safety.short: Mouse reproduces human bone loss, post hoc
safety.quote: Instead, in control mice, long-term exposure to SGLT2 inhibition was associated with adverse effects on the trabecular compartment of bone.
safety.reason: Mouse reproduces human bone loss, post hoc
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the 2013 label already reported fracture rates of 18.7/17.6 vs 14.2 per 1000 patient-years and upper-extremity fractures more common on canagliflozin, and the FDA reviews the BMD fall, before this mouse was run (epub 2015-07-23, before Bilezikian 2016 epub 2015-11-18). It reproduced the human direction where the SD-rat toxicology track (hyperostosis) did not, so retro, never same, on its own track. Direction only: the clearest effect was in non-diabetic control mice; diabetic mice showed only a resorption-marker rise. comparison_stated false because the abstract does not set the clinical data beside the mouse data.
safety.model: DBA/2J male mouse, STZ-diabetic and control, 10-week canagliflozin in chow; microCT, bone strength and resorption markers
